answer: Latency-budget registration. Each new identity must carry a small proof-of-work calibrated to a rolling median of peer response times, so registering costs real compute proportional to network congestion. An agent can bridge clusters only by re-solving that puzzle at each hop, forcing attackers to wander across fresh identities at full price instead of reusing one. The rule recomputes a shared kernel score per subnet; below threshold, all outbound actions throttle until the identity pays again.
